explainers.name: browser
explainers.summary: The app you visit websites with, such as Chrome, Safari or Firefox. It sends the request and draws the page that comes back.

explainers.name: web server
explainers.summary: An always-on computer that answers requests from browsers, running software such as nginx or Apache. For a WordPress page, it hands the work to PHP.

explainers.name: PHP
explainers.summary: The programming language WordPress is written in. The web server asks PHP to run WordPress's code, and that code builds the page.

explainers.name: database
explainers.summary: Where WordPress keeps your content (posts, pages, settings and users) in tables, usually in MySQL or MariaDB. On the map, it's the depot.

explainers.name: index.php
explainers.summary: WordPress's front door: visits to your site's pages start here. The file is tiny; it switches on the theme and loads wp-blog-header.php.

explainers.name: wp-blog-header.php
explainers.summary: Loads WordPress through wp-load.php, runs wp() to work out what was asked for, then loads the theme's template.

explainers.name: wp-load.php
explainers.summary: Notes where WordPress lives on the server, then loads wp-config.php from WordPress's folder or the folder above it. With no config file, it starts the setup instead.

explainers.name: wp-config.php
explainers.summary: Your site's own settings file: the database name, user and password, security keys and options such as WP_DEBUG. It ends by loading wp-settings.php.

explainers.name: wp-settings.php
explainers.summary: The interchange where WordPress sets itself up. It loads core's code, then must-use plugins, plugins and the theme, announcing each stage with a hook.

explainers.name: plugin.php
explainers.summary: Despite the name, this is part of core, not a plugin. It holds the hook functions: add_action, do_action, add_filter, apply_filters and the rest.

explainers.name: class-wp-hook.php
explainers.summary: Defines WP_Hook, the class that keeps each hook's listeners sorted by priority and calls them in that order.

explainers.name: functions.php
explainers.summary: A theme's own file of setup code, loaded while WordPress starts up. With a child theme, the child's functions.php loads first, then the parent's.

explainers.name: muplugins_loaded
explainers.summary: Fires once the must-use plugins, the ones that always run, have loaded. Regular plugins haven't loaded yet.

explainers.name: plugins_loaded
explainers.summary: Fires once every active plugin has loaded. The theme hasn't loaded yet, so it's a plugin's first chance to see all the others.

explainers.name: setup_theme
explainers.summary: Fires just before WordPress sets up and loads the active theme.

explainers.name: after_setup_theme
explainers.summary: Fires right after the theme's functions.php has loaded. Themes use it to switch on features, such as post formats or editor styles.

explainers.name: init
explainers.summary: Fires once plugins and the theme have loaded and the current user is set up, before anything is sent to the browser. Plugins register their content types, blocks and settings here.

explainers.name: wp_loaded
explainers.summary: Fires right after init, once WordPress, every plugin and the theme are fully loaded.

explainers.name: do_action
explainers.summary: Fires an action: it calls every function signed up for that hook, lowest priority first. It hands nothing back.

explainers.name: add_action
explainers.summary: Signs a function up for an action, so WordPress calls it when that hook fires. The optional priority is its ticket number, and the default is 10.

explainers.name: WP_Query
explainers.summary: The class WordPress uses to ask the database for posts. On this visit, it fetches the one post the address points to.

explainers.name: template
explainers.summary: The junction where WordPress picks the template that draws the page. It walks a list from most specific to most general and takes the first one the theme has.

explainers.name: the_title
explainers.summary: A filter: before a theme shows a post's title, WordPress passes the title through every function on the_title, and each one may change it.

explainers.name: 200 OK
explainers.summary: The status code a web server sends when a page worked. A missing page gets 404 Not Found instead.

explainers.name: create_initial_post_types
explainers.summary: Registers WordPress's built-in post types, such as posts, pages, attachments, revisions and block templates, and post statuses like draft and published.

explainers.name: create_initial_taxonomies
explainers.summary: Registers the built-in ways to group posts, such as categories and tags. This run, on init, also gives them pretty addresses like /category/news/.

explainers.name: _wp_register_default_icon_collections
explainers.summary: Registers the core icon collection, labelled WordPress, that the built-in icons belong to. It's new in WordPress 7.1.

explainers.name: wp_initialize_site_preview_hooks
explainers.summary: Checks whether this visit is a site preview: the address asks for one and the visitor may edit the theme. Only then does it mark the page as shown in a frame; on a visit like this one, it does nothing.

explainers.name: hooked_demo_init
explainers.summary: A made-up plugin's listener, here so a plugin's ticket shows on the platform. It does nothing; a real plugin would set itself up here.

explainers.name: twentytwentyfive_block_styles
explainers.summary: From the Twenty Twenty-Five theme: adds a Checkmark style to the List block, so a list can show ticks instead of bullets.

explainers.name: twentytwentyfive_pattern_categories
explainers.summary: From the Twenty Twenty-Five theme: adds two pattern categories, Pages and Post formats, to group the theme's ready-made layouts in the editor.

explainers.name: twentytwentyfive_register_block_bindings
explainers.summary: From the Twenty Twenty-Five theme: registers a block binding source, Post format name, so a block can show the post's format, such as Gallery or Quote.
